stops.note: 'life', as in Suetonius's De vita Caesarum, the Lives of the Caesars
the Polish biochemist Casimir Funk, working at the Lister Institute in London, coined it in 1912 from vita + amine, believing these vital nutrients were all amines
when most turned out not to be amines, Jack Drummond proposed in 1920 dropping the final e

current_meaning: any of a group of organic compounds essential in small amounts for health
